repairs.failure_pattern: Full-image validation or inference fails because a reconstructed image has dimensions derived from another sample and cannot be compared with or cropped to the current document.
repair_steps: Record the native height and width of every image when loading it.
Create reconstruction and overlap-weight accumulators separately for each image using that image's dimensions.
Place or blend patches only within the current image's coordinate bounds.
Crop any padded reconstruction back to the recorded native dimensions before computing RMSE or generating predictions.
Assert that each reconstructed prediction and its clean target have identical shapes before metric computation.
repairs.root_cause: The patch pipeline assumes every document shares a single global height and width, although document images in this task can have different native dimensions.
repairs.title: Provisional: reconstruct each document at its native dimensions
repairs.when_to_use: Use when dataset inspection finds multiple image dimensions or when full-image reconstruction produces prediction-target shape mismatches.

repairs.failure_pattern: A U-Net forward pass fails at a decoder skip concatenation because the upsampled decoder feature and encoder feature have different spatial heights or widths.
repair_steps: Determine the network's total downsampling factor from the number and stride of encoder stages.
Pad input images or patches so both spatial dimensions are divisible by that factor.
At every decoder stage, resize or symmetrically pad or crop the decoder feature to the exact spatial shape of the corresponding encoder feature before concatenation.
After the output layer, crop the prediction back to the original unpadded dimensions.
Run a forward-shape test on representative odd-sized and task-sized inputs before training.
repairs.root_cause: Input padding and decoder upsampling do not preserve the same spatial lattice through all encoder and decoder levels, so corresponding skip tensors are not spatially aligned.
repairs.title: Provisional: align U-Net decoder features with skip tensors before concatenation
repairs.when_to_use: Use when a U-Net or similar encoder-decoder reports unequal spatial sizes at torch.cat or when document dimensions are not naturally divisible by the complete downsampling factor.

repairs.failure_pattern: A decoder or output convolution receives a tensor whose channel count differs from the layer's declared in_channels after upsampling and skip fusion.
repair_steps: Write down the channel width emitted by every encoder, upsampling, concatenation, and decoder block.
For each concatenation, configure the following convolution for the sum of the participating channel widths.
Configure the output head from the actual width emitted by the final decoder block rather than from an earlier concatenated width.
Add assertions for expected channels at skip-fusion boundaries.
Execute a representative dummy forward pass before starting the training loop.
repairs.root_cause: The architecture's channel bookkeeping does not match the forward path; a block is configured for a pre-concatenation or earlier-stage width even though the preceding decoder block emits a different number of channels.
repairs.title: Provisional: derive U-Net convolution inputs from actual concatenated channel counts
repairs.when_to_use: Use when Conv2d reports an expected-versus-actual channel mismatch in a U-Net decoder or output head.

repairs.failure_pattern: NAFNet construction fails before training because the runtime does not provide the requested two-dimensional LayerNorm module.
repair_steps: Check normalization-layer availability in the target runtime before constructing the model.

Replace the unavailable two-dimensional LayerNorm with an available channel-wise normalization implementation compatible with NCHW tensors, such as InstanceNorm2d or an explicit permutation-based LayerNorm wrapper.
Preserve the block's input and output channel count when substituting normalization.
Instantiate the complete NAFNet and run a dummy forward pass before patch training begins.
repairs.root_cause: The model depends on a normalization class that is unavailable in the installed PyTorch API, so encoder blocks cannot be instantiated.
repairs.title: Provisional: use an available channel-wise normalization implementation in NAFNet blocks
repairs.when_to_use: Use when a NAFNet-style denoiser fails during model construction because LayerNorm2d or an equivalent NCHW normalization class is unavailable.

repairs.failure_pattern: Overlapping-patch inference fails while adding a predicted patch into a full-image accumulator because one tensor is on CUDA and the other is on CPU.
repair_steps: Choose one device for reconstruction accumulation before entering the inference loop.
If accumulating on CPU, detach and transfer each predicted patch to CPU before blending it into CPU prediction and weight accumulators.
If accumulating on GPU, allocate both prediction and weight accumulators on the model's device and transfer the completed reconstruction to CPU only after blending.
Ensure coordinate masks, blending weights, and count tensors use the same device as the accumulator.
Assert device equality immediately before each patch accumulation operation.
repairs.root_cause: Predicted patches are transferred between devices independently of the reconstruction and overlap-count tensors, violating the single-device requirement for tensor arithmetic.
repairs.title: Provisional: keep patch predictions and reconstruction accumulators on one device
repairs.when_to_use: Use when test or validation reconstruction blends model outputs into full-image tensors and runtime errors report tensors on different devices.

repairs.failure_pattern: Training initialization fails when constructing a linear warmup scheduler because its multiplicative start factor is zero or outside the scheduler's accepted interval.
repair_steps: Set the warmup start factor to a small positive value within the scheduler's valid interval, such as 0.001 or 0.01.
Set the end factor to a valid value, normally 1.0, and use a positive warmup iteration count.
Construct the warmup scheduler before training and inspect its first and final warmup learning rates.
When chaining warmup with cosine decay, align scheduler milestones with the intended number of warmup epochs.
repairs.root_cause: LinearLR represents learning rates as positive factors of the optimizer's base rate and requires the starting factor to be greater than zero and no greater than one.
repairs.title: Provisional: configure linear learning-rate warmup with a valid positive start factor
repairs.when_to_use: Use when an image-denoising training pipeline uses LinearLR warmup and scheduler construction rejects start_factor=0 or another out-of-range factor.
